releases.notes:
Minecraft 26.3 is now supported. Download `shapeboard-1.7.1+26.3.jar` and use Java 25, Fabric Loader 0.19.5 or newer, and Fabric API for 26.3.

Existing shapes and totals are retained when updating the same world. Stop the server cleanly, back up the world, replace the old ShapeBoard jar and update Fabric as needed. Keep the world's `shapeboard/` folder and vanilla scoreboard data. There is no need to recreate shapes or rescan them to resume counting.

The volume scanner now reads Minecraft 26.3's string and `id` block palettes as well as older `Name` palettes. This fixes scans reporting zero remaining blocks after a world upgrade. The English and Spanish READMEs include the compatibility table and update instructions.

Validation: all 14 supported jars compile. A local Fabric 26.2 world using ShapeBoard 1.7.0 was upgraded to Fabric 26.3 with ShapeBoard 1.7.1. Four shapes across two dimensions, 18 individual break/placement scores, baselines, scan snapshots and player preferences were retained; 40 command responses matched. A fresh scan counted the expected 300 blocks, including a mixed palette with 190 stone, 100 diamond ore and 10 stairs, and a second restart retained the data. The placement mixin was also verified in the runtime-transformed `BlockItem` class.

Earlier Minecraft versions remain supported, from 1.21 through 26.2. Choose the jar whose filename matches your Minecraft version; the `+1.21` jar also covers 1.21.1 and `+26.1.2` also covers 26.1 and 26.1.1.

releases.notes:
ShapeBoard now runs on every Minecraft release from **1.21 to 26.2**. Nothing the mod does changed in this version: it is the same 1.6.0 feature set, built for thirteen versions instead of eight.

## Which jar do I download

Grab the one that ends in your Minecraft version. A jar refuses to load on a version it was not built for, rather than half working.

| Minecraft | Jar | Java |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1.21, 1.21.1 | `shapeboard-1.7.0+1.21.jar` | 21 |
| 1.21.2 | `shapeboard-1.7.0+1.21.2.jar` | 21 |
| 1.21.3 | `shapeboard-1.7.0+1.21.3.jar` | 21 |
| 1.21.4 | `shapeboard-1.7.0+1.21.4.jar` | 21 |
| 1.21.5 | `shapeboard-1.7.0+1.21.5.jar` | 21 |
| 1.21.6 | `shapeboard-1.7.0+1.21.6.jar` | 21 |
| 1.21.7 | `shapeboard-1.7.0+1.21.7.jar` | 21 |
| 1.21.8 | `shapeboard-1.7.0+1.21.8.jar` | 21 |
| 1.21.9 | `shapeboard-1.7.0+1.21.9.jar` | 21 |
| 1.21.10 | `shapeboard-1.7.0+1.21.10.jar` | 21 |
| 1.21.11 | `shapeboard-1.7.0+1.21.11.jar` | 21 |
| 26.1, 26.1.1, 26.1.2 | `shapeboard-1.7.0+26.1.2.jar` | 25 |
| 26.2 | `shapeboard-1.7.0+26.2.jar` | 25 |

New here: 1.21.9, 1.21.10, 1.21.11, 26.1, 26.1.1, 26.1.2 and 26.2. Minecraft 26.1 and up need Java 25, which is the game's requirement rather than the mod's.

## New to ShapeBoard

Track blocks broken and placed inside **any** shape you outline with marker blocks in the sky, not just a box, with a leaderboard sidebar that only the people standing inside the area see. Server side only: your players join with a vanilla client and install nothing. Full walkthrough in the [README](https://github.com/CodeW4VE/ShapeBoard#readme).

If you are tracking a build rather than a dig, remember step 4 of the quick start: `/shapeboard metric <id> place` ranks by blocks placed, and `both` by the sum.

## For anyone reading the source

The mod used to ship out of three branches, one per point where Minecraft renamed an API. That does not survive seven more versions, and 26.x cannot share a build script with 1.21 at all, since Minecraft stopped shipping obfuscated in 26.1 and there are no mappings left to ask for.

All thirteen jars now come out of `main` via `tools/multiversion.py`: the renames live in one substitution table, and the 26.x build script is derived from the 1.21 one rather than kept next to it. Everything the ports actually needed was renaming, which is why the table is short:

- **1.21.5** chat click and hover events became records, and every NBT getter returns an `Optional` with an `OrElse` twin beside it
- **1.21.11** `ResourceLocation` is `Identifier`, `ResourceKey.location()` is `identifier()`, and a command's permission level is `Commands.hasPermission(Commands.LEVEL_GAMEMASTERS)`
- **26.1** Loom no longer remaps anything, Java 25, mixins compiled to match

Checked on real servers rather than only by compiling: 1.21.11 and 26.2 both boot, register their commands, and count a volume scan to the block, with the same numbers on both.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/CodeW4VE/ShapeBoard/compare/v1.6.0...v1.7.0

releases.notes:
## How much is left before we reach y?

Layer by layer was already there, but the question crews actually plan around is *"how much before this thing is clear down to y-20?"*. That is a sum over layers, and the volume scan already stores every one of them, so it costs nothing to answer.

- **`/shapeboard down <y> [id]`** — adds up every block still standing from the top of the scan down to that Y. Progress bar, blocks cleared and remaining, and how many of those layers are done.

```
— Big Culo · down to y-20 —
███████░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 38.60%
Down to y-20: 210,455 / 545,180 blocks cleared, 334,725 remaining
Layers: 43 of 96 cleared from y99 down to y-20, highest one left is y41.
```

It reads from the last `/shapeboard scan` like `progress` and `layer` do, so it answers instantly and does not touch the world. With no `id` it uses the shape you are standing in.

Thanks to the player who suggested it.

releases.notes:
## Two boards in one zone

A zone that gets **dug out first and built up later** needed two leaderboards in the same place. It turns out it already had them: breaks and placements were always counted into two separate objectives, only the view was missing.

- **`/shapeboard view <break|place|both|reset>`** — any player, any time, picks what **their own** sidebar ranks by, whatever the zone is set to. Saved across sessions. A builder can watch the placements while the diggers keep their board.
- **`/shapeboard suffix <id> <word|auto|off>`** and **`/shapeboard prefix <id> <word|off>`** — decorate the sidebar title. `auto` resolves to **Dig**, **Build** or **Both** following what each viewer is ranking by, so "Virusia" reads *Virusia Dig* during the dig phase and *Virusia Build* on building day.

Overlapping shapes were never the answer (a column belongs to the first shape that contains it), and now they are not needed.

## Fewer messages

- **`/shapeboard quiet [on|off]`** — mutes the entered/left chat lines for good. The sidebar keeps working.
- Those lines are now **rate limited to one per zone every 15 minutes**, and the hint below them only shows the first time. Crossing the border of a big perimeter happens a lot more often than anyone wants to read about it.

## Fixed

- A brand new shape showed **nothing at all**: a sidebar with zero lines is not drawn by the client, so the board looked broken until the first block was counted. It now renders the zeroed board.

releases.notes:
## What is actually left in there

People planning storage kept asking the same thing: not "how much is left" but **what** is left. `/shapeboard blocks` answers it.

```
/shapeboard blocks

— Big Culo blocks left —
deepslate 37,376,792
stone 32,912,885
tuff 3,131,119
andesite 3,086,276
...
other 48,445
Blocks left: 88,659,548 in 40 listed types
```

Snapshots now remember 40 block types instead of 5, so the list covers everything that matters and lumps the tail into `other`. No argument uses the zone you are standing in, same as `progress` and `layer`.

On our own perimeter it turns out two block types, deepslate and stone, are 79% of the entire job, and the ore total is 1.15M blocks. That is the kind of thing you want to know *before* building the storage hall.
